doc.title: Candido Camero — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Birth in El Cerro, parents, siblings and father's factory job
summary: Camero gives his birth date and place in Havana, his parents' and siblings' names, and says his father made soft-drink bottles while his mother stayed at home.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Candido Camero: Well, from my birth - I was born on Friday, April 22, 1921 at six thirty in the afternoon in El Cerro, one of the neighborhoods in the city of Havana, Cuba. My dad’s name is Candido Camero. My mom’s name is Caridad Guerra.

And do you have brothers and sisters, and what are their respective names? Candido: Well, my sister who follows me in age, her name is Elena Camero - Elena Camero Guerra. My brother who follows my sister in age is Virgilio Camero Guerra. And the youngest of all my brothers is Faustino Camero Guerra. Only my sister and I are still living. My mom died, my dad died, my two brothers passed and only my sister and I are left.
Tell me maestro, what did your father do to make a living?
My dad worked in a factory making bottles for soft drinks in Cuba. He worked at the factory. My mother worked only at home. She attended to us, raised us, but never worked - only my dad.
